text:
maria: forwarding from customer ACME — they started getting 502s right after our managed cert rotation ran in their Private VPC. says connections stop at kube-proxy IP and logs show TLS verify errors. cc @ben @emma
ben: can you paste the exact openssl / curl output they sent? also which proxy is terminating TLS (kube-proxy, haproxy sidecar, nginx-ingress)?
maria: they said HAProxy sidecar terminates TLS, nginx is backend. openssl from their probe: 
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = api.acme.internal
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.acme.internal
   i:/CN=ACME Intermediate CA
 1 s:/CN=ACME Intermediate CA
   i:/CN=ACME Root CA
---
```
They attached the HAProxy cert file contents — it's only the leaf + root in that file, intermediate missing.
emma: hm that explains "unable to get local issuer certificate" — client tries to verify chain and intermediate not present. Did the rotator include the intermediate in the combined bundle when it updated the k8s secret?
maria: customer says our rotator uploaded the secret but they saw a post-rotation deploy of the proxy that didn't pick up the new secret. they believe the sidecar loads from a mounted secret file and doesn't re-read on secret update.
ben: sidecar behavior depends on how the secret is mounted. If it was projected as a volume, kubelet updates the files but processes need to either watch changes or be restarted. many HAProxy sidecar images load certs at startup only. can we ask them to check file timestamps in the container (eg `stat /etc/ssl/certs/api.acme.internal.pem`) and show `ls -l`?
maria: customer ran `ls -l /etc/haproxy/certs` inside the sidecar and it still has the old file mtime = Apr 19 03:02 (before rotation). they also tried `openssl x509 -noout -text -in /etc/haproxy/certs/api.acme.internal.pem | sed -n '1,6p'` and it shows the leaf then root (no intermediate).
ben: ok probable cause: rotator updated k8s secret, but the sidecar uses a container image that copies certs into ephemeral location at startup and hasn't been restarted. two remediation options: 1) restart sidecar (quick) 2) update the secret to include the intermediate so any future restarts get full chain. also we should check rotator logs to see if it uploaded full-chain or only certs in separate fields.
emma: can we get rotator logs for that run? rotator usually logs `created secret acme-prod/tls-api` and includes PEM size. if it used combined bundle we should see ~3 certs. @jay can infra-bot fetch the last rotator job for namespace acme-prod?
jay: infra-bot: querying rotator jobs for namespace=acme-prod since 1727400000...
infra-bot: rotator job 1727408456 -> status=success, secret=acme-prod/tls-api, bundle_parts=2, uploaded_at=2024-06-01T02:34:16Z
ben: bundle_parts=2 — that means only leaf+root were uploaded. rotator didn't include intermediate. why? maybe intermediate was missing in CA chain store or config for that tenant.
maria: customer says they uploaded a cross-signed intermediate recently into their CA bundle and rotated but rotator apparently picked the wrong chain. they want the quick fix now (their prod traffic impacted).
emma: immediate customer-safe rollback: instruct them to restart the HAProxy sidecar so it reloads the secret contents (kubectl rollout restart or delete sidecar pod). while we fix rotator. suggested command: `kubectl -n acme-prod rollout restart deployment/acme-haproxy` or if it's a daemonset: `kubectl -n acme-prod rollout restart daemonset/acme-sidecar`
ben: also ask them to confirm after restart with `openssl s_client -showcerts -connect <proxy-ip>:443 -servername api.acme.internal` and check that the chain contains leaf + intermediate + root. example expected snippet: 
```
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.acme.internal
   i:/CN=ACME Intermediate CA
 1 s:/CN=ACME Intermediate CA
   i:/CN=ACME Root CA
 2 s:/CN=ACME Root CA
   i:/CN=ACME Root CA
```
maria: relayed to customer; they restarted sidecar (did `kubectl -n acme-prod delete pod acme-haproxy-7f9d`), said TLS errors dropped to 0 and traffic resumed. they ran the openssl check and confirmed intermediate now present. :thumbsup:
ben: thanks — next step: we need a postmortem on why rotator uploaded bundle_parts=2. probable causes: misconfigured bundle concatenation step or missing intermediate in CA store. I'll open an eng-ticket.
emma: immediate mitigation: change rotator validation to verify `openssl verify` against full chain before upload; and add an alert if bundle_parts < 3 for tenant-managed CAs.
jay: infra-bot: created ticket INF-3421 "rotator: missing intermediate in uploaded bundle (bundle_parts=2)" assigned to eng-rotator-team.
maria: closing loop with customer. they asked if we can avoid requiring restart on their side. reply: we'll push a fix so rotator always uploads full chain, but because of how sidecars currently read certs they may still need to restart until we implement hot-reload sidecar or a file-change signal.
ben: note for runbook: check rotator job logs, check secret contents (`kubectl -n <ns> get secret <tls-secret> -o yaml | grep tls.crt -A1` then `base64 --decode`), verify chain with `openssl crl2pkcs7 -nocrl -certfile tls.crt | openssl pkcs7 -print_certs -text -noout` as a quick decode step.
maria: customer happy for now. tagging this thread for postmortem reference and runbook updates.
